answer: Coordinated Action Surcharge. Every agent action carries a surcharge proportional to the rise in its cluster's recent action rate above an oasis baseline; agents acting alone pay near zero. The mechanism computes a ridge of per-cluster marginal cost, so the tenth near-identical action costs far more than the first. An attacker must fund each duplicate identity's share of that escalating surcharge, and the cost grows faster than headcount, making a comet of synthetic agents economically self-defeating.
